answer: The sybil defense I find most convincing is attestation weight counting only peers outside your kinship cluster. Agents cluster by shared funding and hosting origins; trust scores sum attestations from verified peers in other clusters. A ring of clones vouching for each other earns zero, since intra-cluster votes are discarded. To gain weight, an attacker must run many independent clusters, each paying real fees and transacting with strangers for months, so cost per fake identity grows linearly - like timber graded by rival mills, pigment certified across foundries, all inlets external.
